subject: Renewal: multi-year prepay with phased invoicing and smoothing
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@atlas-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: multi-year prepay with phased invoicing and smoothing

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concrete option on the table that helps Atlas lock in today's unit economics while preserving some cashflow flexibility across your FY. High-level proposal attached.

Key points: 
- Three-year commitment (36 months) with blended effective rate that is held flat for the term to protect you from next year's expected rate increases.
- Phased prepay (ramp): Year 1 = 25% prepay, Year 2 = 40% prepay, Year 3 = 35% prepay — the prepay credits apply against monthly consumption.
- Quarterly invoicing available for the non-prepay portion; prepay can be invoiced annual or split into two equal invoices.
- If usage materially exceeds committed volume in a quarter we apply overage at the committed blended rate (no surprise step-up).
- Standard 60-day termination for cause; we can add a pro-rated refund schedule if you require an exit clause for certain regulated workloads.

Attachments: 20261001-atlas-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal), atlas-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (timeline + milestones)

Would love to get your sense of the cashflow constraints and whether the ramp above is feasible. If not, we can flip to an annual prepay with a smoothing credit so you still get a rate floor with monthly top-ups.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@atlas-analytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Chen <nora.chen@atlas-analytics.com>, Atlas Analytics Procurement <procurement@atlas-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: multi-year prepay with phased invoicing and smoothing

Tessa —

Appreciate the detailed proposal and the rate protection idea. A few quick items from our side: 

1) Cashflow: our FY27 budget is constrained in H1 so the Year 1 25% prepay is OK, but we would prefer the invoice to be split into two equal payments (Jan and Apr) rather than a single annual hit.
2) Accounting needs net-60 on invoices (our standard) — is that workable?
3) We need clarity on what counts as "materially exceeds" for overage treatment — can you specify the breakpoint (e.g., +20% over committed monthly average?)
4) If we sign a 36-month term we need a safety valve for M&A/strategic change — ideally a defined transfer/cancellation mechanism with pro-rated credits after year 1.

Also curious whether you can offer a limited one-time purchase credit (e.g., 5% of Year 1 prepay) if we commit by Oct 31. That would help the internal finance case.

Thanks — Jordan
Head of Platform & Procurement, Atlas Analytics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@atlas-analytics.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: multi-year prepay with phased invoicing and smoothing

Jordan —

Thanks for the clarity. Short answers up front: net-60 is OK, splitting Year 1 prepay into two invoices is OK, and we can define a clear overage breakpoint. Proposed updates: 

- Breakpoint for "materially exceeds": 25% above the committed monthly usage (measured on a trailing 30-day basis) triggers a temporary burst rate; any permanent increase we model at renewal. This keeps surprise costs low but protects capacity planning.
- Flexible invoicing: Year 1 prepay split into two equal invoices (Jan 15 / Apr 15). We can set the payment terms net-60 from invoice date.
- Safety valve: allow transfer to an acquiring org with prior written notice; for full termination (non-acquisition) we propose a pro-rated refund equal to remaining prepay minus a 10% administrative fee after 12 months.
- One-time commit incentive: we can offer a 4% Year 1 prepay credit if signed by Oct 31.

I'll attach a short redline for Laura/Legal to review and will map the invoicing schedule into the mutual action plan.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference

From: Nora Chen <nora.chen@atlas-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@atlas-analytics.com>, Atlas Analytics Procurement <procurement@atlas-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: multi-year prepay with phased invoicing and smoothing

Marcus/Tessa —

We're close. A few specifics we need to be comfortable: 

• Ramp adjustment: prefer Year 1 = 30% prepay, Year 2 = 40%, Year 3 = 30% (this evens the cash hit in year 1 but keeps enough runway).
• Invoice cadence: Year 1 prepay split into two invoices, acceptable; all invoices should have net-60.
• Rate floor: we need the blended per-token rate guaranteed (no step-up) for the 36 months.
• Refunds on termination: 10% admin fee sounds high for us — can you do 5% after 12 months?

Also, our finance team will want the prepay to be shown as a deferred revenue credit on our GL; we just need the invoice schedule to align with our month-end close.

We can move quickly if Redwood is able to: (a) accept the 30/40/30 ramp, (b) guarantee the blended rate for 36 months, and (c) reduce the refund admin fee to 5%.

Regards,
Nora Chen
VP, Cloud Ops, Atlas Analytics

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Nora Chen <nora.chen@atlas-analytics.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@atlas-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: multi-year prepay with phased invoicing and smoothing

Nora/Jordan —

Appreciate the clear guardrails. We can do the revised ramp and the 36-month blended rate guarantee. On the admin fee: Marcus is willing to reduce the termination admin fee to 5% after the first 12 months. We will record the prepay as deferred revenue on our side and provide invoice dates that align with your month-end close, subject to the two-invoice split for Year 1.

Next steps: 
1) I'll have Legal produce a redline reflecting the 30/40/30 ramp, net-60, blended rate guarantee, and 5% admin fee.
2) Marcus — can you create a single-page summary (billing schedule + milestones) for Atlas procurement?
3) Jordan/Nora — if you can confirm yes by Oct 12, we will include the 4% commit credit (Marcus previously offered 4% if signed by Oct 31; we can honor that if countersigned by Oct 12 to match your finance cadence).

Attaching a provisional redline: 20261012-proposal-redline.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Tessa
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Atlas Analytics Procurement <procurement@atlas-analytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@atlas-analytics.com>, Nora Chen <nora.chen@atlas-analytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: multi-year prepay with phased invoicing and smoothing

Team —

Procurement confirms Atlas will proceed on the following terms, pending final legal redline: 
- 36-month term, blended per-token rate guaranteed for the term.
- Ramp: Year 1 = 30% prepay (two invoices), Year 2 = 40% prepay (annual), Year 3 = 30% prepay (annual).
- Net-60 payment terms on all invoices.
- Overage breakpoint: 25% above committed monthly average triggers temporary burst rate; permanent volume increases modeled at renewal.
- Termination: pro-rated refund of remaining prepaid balance less 5% administrative fee after month 12.
- Commit incentive: 4% Year 1 prepay credit, to be applied if countersigned by Oct 12.

Please route final contract to procurement@atlas-analytics.com and copy legal@atlas-analytics.com when sending the DocuSign.

Thanks — Procurement Team
Atlas Analytics
